questions.q: What does a column alias actually change?
options: Only the column header shown in the query's output, not the table itself
The column's name in the underlying table permanently
The data type of the column
Which rows are returned
questions.explain: An alias is purely cosmetic for that query's result set — the table's real column name is untouched.

questions.q: Which keyword introduces a column alias?
options: AS
ALIAS
RENAME
TO
questions.explain: SELECT column AS alias_name — AS is the standard keyword, though T-SQL also allows omitting it.

questions.q: Why does this course always write AS explicitly, even though T-SQL allows omitting it?
options: Omitting it is easy to misread, especially if a comma is missing between columns
SQL Server throws an error without it
AS improves query performance
It's required in AdventureWorks2012 specifically
questions.explain: Dropping AS still works, but 'FirstName GivenName' next to a missing comma can silently merge two intended columns into one aliased one.

questions.q: Why would you alias an expression like ListPrice * 0.9?
options: Without an alias, SQL Server gives the calculated column an unreadable, unnamed header
Expressions cannot be selected without an alias
It changes the calculation's result
It's required only for aggregate functions
questions.explain: A calculated expression has no natural column name, so an alias is what makes the result set readable.

questions.q: How do you write an alias that contains a space, like 'Given Name'?
options: Wrap it in square brackets: AS [Given Name]
Use an underscore instead of a space
Spaces in aliases are not allowed under any circumstances
Wrap it in parentheses: AS (Given Name)
questions.explain: Square brackets quote an identifier so it can contain spaces or reserved words.
